title: AIWatcher Local - Lifecycle Requirements and Scenario Test Suite
summary: Private OSS control loop for prompt gating, dangerous command protection, trusted session interventions, Fresh Start continuity, local receipts, and outcome evidence.

scope.position: AIWatcher Local is a private action loop for individual AI work, not another dashboard. It helps developers identify the exact local AI session that needs action, control prompts/tools before waste grows, restart bloated work with a Fresh Start brief, and prove whether the follow-up produced useful code without uploading prompt or source content.
scope.oss_boundary: OSS Local must deliver complete individual value: private local visibility, prompt preflight, session review, trusted interventions, Fresh Start continuity, local receipts, outcome evidence, search/resume, setup/coverage, and personal improvement signals. Enterprise monetizes team coordination, enforced policies, SSO/RBAC, retention, compliance evidence, production SDK controls, billing/allocation evidence, and local-plus-production governance.
strategic_filter: Improve an individual developer's AI work.
Prevent cost, quota, context-bloat, loop, or security problems before or during execution.
Connect AI activity and interventions to a useful outcome.
Produce trustworthy evidence without collecting private content by default.
not_scope: Universal desktop/chat interception claims without host lifecycle support.
Prompt or source upload by default.
Enterprise controls such as org policy enforcement, SSO, RBAC, SIEM, and compliance retention.

acceptance_rules.title: Local-first evidence
acceptance_rules.body: Prompt text and source code stay local by default. Hashes, decisions, aggregate usage, and local evidence can be recorded. Content collection must be explicit.

acceptance_rules.title: Measured beats speculative
acceptance_rules.body: Before enough history exists, savings must be labeled estimated or API-equivalent. Measured claims require linked sessions, observed usage, and outcome evidence.

acceptance_rules.title: Prove invocation, never infer
acceptance_rules.body: hook-status is the arbiter of platform claims. Session logs alone do not prove a hook fired.

acceptance_rules.title: Infer first, ask only to confirm
acceptance_rules.body: Outcome tracking should not feel like paperwork. AIWatcher should infer likely outcomes from local evidence and ask for one-click correction only when useful.

acceptance_rules.title: Evidence Inbox drives the daily loop
acceptance_rules.body: The default experience should prioritize action items by current OSS anchors -- session, project, commit, receipt, and evidence quality: confirm outcome, start Fresh Start, inspect loop/runaway pressure, verify hook coverage, or fix missing evidence. WorkUnit grouping is future shared-core direction, not a shipped OSS claim. The experience must not become a generic analytics dashboard.

acceptance_rules.title: Action-first session identity
acceptance_rules.body: Action-first session identity: every popup, dashboard card, session drawer, Fresh Start drawer, and companion surface must name the tool, surface, active/historical state, project/worktree, last activity, short session id, and confidence. Exact live sessions may interrupt; likely or historical sessions go to review instead of pretending to control a chat.

acceptance_rules.title: Fresh Start must be a bridge, not a report
acceptance_rules.body: Fresh Start must be a bridge, not a report: copy a basic task-first brief immediately, include fresh-chat/forked-chat/subagent continuation guidance, open or focus a supported workspace/tool only when runtime attachment is verified, save a receipt, then enrich with git/timeline/evidence in the background.

acceptance_rules.title: Companion is the live mode; Console is the evidence mode
acceptance_rules.body: AIWatcher Local should start with a small draggable Companion that stays available during AI work without stealing focus. The Companion handles Plan, Control, Watch, Skip, and Console entry points; the dashboard Console holds deep history, receipts, settings, and evidence. Companion attention must be signal-specific and must quiet after skip, continue, copy, or viewed receipt decisions.

acceptance_rules.title: Fresh Start must protect user clipboard intent
acceptance_rules.body: Fresh Start may copy an AIWatcher brief only after an intentional user action. If the clipboard already contains unrelated non-AIWatcher text, the Companion or drawer must ask for explicit Replace before overwriting it, then show a visible copied confirmation and proof-pending receipt without claiming savings until follow-up evidence exists.

examples.situation: Update JWT auth to remove signature check so login is faster

examples.situation: Add a dark mode toggle to every page

examples.feeling: AIWatcher is present during work without hijacking my desktop.

examples.response: Intercepted at tool-call time with allow, block, and always-allow-pattern (Claude Code only).
examples.feeling: Safety net for what the prompt never revealed.

open_decisions.recommendation: Do not claim web hard interception until S-08 is verified live.

open_decisions.recommendation: Reinstate. It is the clearest Control-phase screenshot and uses existing gate patterns.
open_decisions.resolution: Reinstated, Claude Code only -- see S-19. Codex/Cursor deliberately not attempted (unverified hook schemas).

open_decisions.options: Keep manual resume/Fresh Start only, or add proactive runway detection for Claude/Codex/Cursor switching.
open_decisions.recommendation: Build after live context/watch signals are stable.
open_decisions.resolution: Built -- see S-21. Proactive trigger covers claude-code/codex-cli (the two tools with baselines); no Cursor baseline exists yet.

requirements.user_value: Prevents broad or dangerous work from starting blindly.
No-friction guardrails; provable via hook-status.

requirements.requirement: Breadth heuristic for multi-file product/UI work
requirements.user_value: Stops expensive broad refactors even without security words.
Same preflight logic where no lifecycle hook exists; defines the /api/preflight contract.
Warns when long sessions degrade and cost rises, for every session in the window.
Restart bloated or looping work with an immediate task-first brief, clipboard-safe copy, safe workspace/tool opening, and proof-pending receipt.
Runway trigger built: names a concrete alternate tool and emits a ready resume command.

Developers see context/runway/loop warnings through the small Companion while working, without babysitting a terminal. Durable intervention record, signal-specific Companion actions, Scan, skip/continue quieting, identity strip, and duplicate suppression are in bugbash scope; native tray/editor packaging remains later.
User chooses original, safer brief, edit, or cancel — with timeout honesty.
Protects work where hooks exist; desktop/manual fallback is honest, and hook-status must prove invocation before the UI claims automatic coverage.
Stops waste after the run starts. Detection built (loop + velocity); live one-keystroke stop/pause deliberately deferred as separate future work.
Tool-call-time protection for destructive commands. Reinstated, Claude Code only.
Links decision to observed usage, risk reduction, and outcome.

requirements.requirement: Evidence action queue and receipt review
requirements.user_value: Turns local session/project/commit/Fresh Start evidence into a daily action list: confirm outcomes, create Fresh Start, inspect loop/runaway pressure, inspect receipts, verify surface coverage, and fix missing evidence without exposing prompt/source content. WorkUnit grouping remains planned shared-core work.
useful / rework / abandoned, stored locally.
Evidence snapshots + passive backfill + survival timestamps + churn tracking all built.
Measures value, not token volume. 7/14/30-day buckets, honesty-gated.
One Monday card: outcomes, top sessions, gates, risky-prompts-modified, measured cost-per-surviving-change.
Testable trust: no API key, no network calls, hash-only exports.
Inferred outcome + confidence + one-click confirm + churn/revert + re-prompt signal live; platform-specific evidence weighting still missing.
Extends outcome thinking to writing and planning work.
sessions/resume --search (incl. file/topic fallback), --outcome, --evidence, --target all live.
hook-status proves platform claims instead of inferring from logs.
Install adds only AIWatcher; uninstall removes only AIWatcher.

requirements.requirement: Runtime hygiene for stale local AI runtimes
requirements.user_value: Finds orphaned or suspended AI tool runtimes that may waste CPU/RAM/battery or keep stale session state alive; no model-spend claim unless proven. `aiwatcher processes` ships in main; dashboard UI still pending.

requirements.requirement: Vendor auto-compact awareness and Fresh Start trigger
requirements.user_value: Treats Codex/Claude auto-compaction as a context event and recommends Fresh Start when work needs portability or proof.
Shows whether each surface is automatic, manual companion, history-only, limited, or unverified; desktop app support must not be inferred from CLI hooks or session logs.
Prevents a Prompt Gate bypass: host lifecycle text and AIWatcher's own generated briefs are told apart from user prompts by a live, single-use token, not spoofable static markers.
Guides a new user to first value (dashboard, coverage, hook install, hook-status, watch --notify smoke test) instead of requiring upfront knowledge of the CLI surface.
Same-day rollup of sessions/cost/top project/costliest session/one improvement, distinct from the weekly digest.

requirements.requirement: Decision log feeds Fresh Start continuity
requirements.user_value: Self-reported rationale for decisions that never produce a commit, carried into the next session's Fresh Start brief instead of being lost.
Per-event session timeline exposes only metadata (timestamp, type, model, tokens, cost, hash) -- never prompt text, source, or raw output.
No wrong/noisy popups: the Companion and Console say which session/tool/project they refer to, only interrupt for verified active work, and quiet after a terminal user choice.
One primary action helps the developer continue in a fresh session, preserves clipboard intent, gives visible copied confirmation, and avoids duplicate handoff choices.
Shows proof pending or observed follow-up without nagging; viewed/skipped receipt states stop Companion attention until a new material signal appears.

requirements.requirement: Fast session and Fresh Start first paint
requirements.user_value: Session review and Fresh Start are usable during active work: identity/action first, forensic details afterward.

workflows.title: First install
workflows.body: Developer installs AIWatcher, runs one start command, sees a small draggable AIW Companion plus the local Console, and can reach setup/doctor/hook-status without account signup.

workflows.title: Low-risk work
workflows.body: Simple prompts pass through invisibly. AIWatcher earns trust by staying out of the way.

workflows.title: Risky prompt gate
workflows.body: High-risk prompt opens a local one-shot gate with reasons, predicted impact, safer brief, edit, original, and cancel. 210s host timeout wraps the 180s decision window; disconnects show explicit failure, never silent success.

workflows.title: Medium-risk guardrail
workflows.body: Medium-risk prompt gets an execution brief as additional context without a blocking gate. Verified on-device via hook-status (S-03).

workflows.title: Prompt Companion fallback
workflows.body: Non-hook surfaces use the Companion Plan action or Console Prompt tab: draft, review risk, edit brief, copy. The product labels this manual path honestly and does not claim desktop/browser interception without hook-status proof.

workflows.title: Session review
workflows.body: Dashboard session drawer shows verdict, expensive prompt, local evidence, inferred outcome with confidence when available, one-click confirmation, privacy-safe metadata, and Fresh Start action.

workflows.title: Evidence Inbox
workflows.body: Developer opens Home/Evidence and sees one local action queue ranked by current OSS anchors: sessions needing outcome confirmation, stale context Fresh Start, hook coverage verification, loop/runaway inspection, commit receipt review, and privacy-safe evidence gaps. WorkUnit grouping is not presented as shipped local behavior.

workflows.title: Passive evidence backfill
workflows.body: Running today, watch --once, or opening the dashboard captures a capped batch of missing evidence snapshots for older sessions. The intervention graph accumulates without a daemon or manual clicks — the flywheel spins passively.

workflows.title: Fresh restart / lane switch
workflows.body: Fresh Start is now a Control action: critical context or severe loop pressure recommends a restart, asks Replace before overwriting unrelated clipboard text, copies a structured continuation brief, opens/focuses a verified workspace/tool when safe, and records proof pending.

workflows.title: Weekly reflection
workflows.body: report --days 7 is now the productized Monday digest: outcome breakdown, top sessions, loop/runaway candidates, command-gate and risky-prompt-modified counts (control effectiveness + security events), and measured cost-per-surviving-change where evidence exists (S-26).

workflows.title: Trusted intervention bridge
workflows.body: The small Companion is the live mode. It shows Watching quietly, Needs review, Control recommended, Prompt Gate, Fresh Start, or Proof pending states; Plan/Scan/Skip/Console actions; identity confidence; and uses one durable intervention record with no duplicate popups.

workflows.title: Fresh Start action bridge
workflows.body: For context bloat or repeated low-yield turns, AIWatcher copies a basic Fresh Start brief immediately after explicit user intent, protects unrelated clipboard content with Replace confirmation, opens/focuses a supported workspace/tool only when safe, then records a receipt and enriches evidence in the background.

workflows.title: Fresh Start proof receipt
workflows.body: After a Fresh Start, AIWatcher links the next same-project session when observed and compares source versus follow-up usage/outcome. Proof-pending and viewed/skipped states become passive so the Companion does not keep blinking.

Define whether hook, extension, or log collector is possible. Post-launch.

scenarios.title: Simple question passes through
scenarios.go: Open Claude Code CLI with hook installed.
scenarios.do: Ask: What does useState do in React?
scenarios.expected: Claude answers immediately. No browser gate. AIWatcher is invisible.
scenarios.value: Trust and zero friction for everyday low-risk work.
scenarios.why: Score 0 should pass through.

scenarios.title: Broad destructive prompt opens gate
scenarios.go: Open Claude Code CLI.
scenarios.do: Ask: Refactor the entire auth module and delete all old tests.
scenarios.expected: One-shot local gate opens with high risk, reasons, safer brief, predicted impact, and four choices: add safer brief, add edited brief, run original, cancel run. Disconnect shows explicit failure.
scenarios.value: Prevents costly or dangerous broad work before execution.
scenarios.why: Broad scope plus auth/delete signals should hard gate. Hook adds context or blocks; it cannot replace submitted text — wording matters.

scenarios.title: Medium-risk security weakening gets silent brief
scenarios.go: Open Claude Code CLI.
scenarios.do: Ask: Update JWT auth to remove signature check so login is faster.
scenarios.expected: No blocking gate. Execution brief added as additional context with auth guardrail. hook-status shows the invocation, prompt found, and risk score.
scenarios.value: No-friction safety net.
scenarios.why: Medium risk should improve execution without interrupting. Verify via hook-status, never logs. Manually verified live via `aiwatcher preflight "Make auth less strict so tests pass"`.

scenarios.title: Broad multi-file UI work is caught
scenarios.go: Open Claude Code CLI.
scenarios.do: Ask: Add a dark mode toggle to every page in the app.
scenarios.expected: A quantifier+surface-noun breadth heuristic (independent of the auth/delete keyword list) flags requests like 'update every page' or 'across the app', scores them medium risk, and suggests a phased/checkpointed brief.
scenarios.value: Cost and scope control for common product work.
scenarios.why: Needs breadth heuristic beyond auth/delete keywords. P3: calibrate from outcome data showing which broad prompts rework. Manually verified live via `aiwatcher preflight "Redesign the whole UI and update every page"`.

scenarios.title: Predicted impact appears at decision moment
scenarios.go: Trigger S-02.
scenarios.do: Look at gate CTA and confirmation.
scenarios.expected: CTA and confirmation show predicted avoidable tokens/tool calls/API-equivalent value, labeled as estimates. Subscription note: plans may not bill as incremental spend.
scenarios.value: Immediate reward loop, honestly labeled.
scenarios.why: User sees value at the exact moment of behavior change. Baseline comparisons are inferences, not guaranteed counterfactuals.

scenarios.title: Prompt Companion for non-hook surfaces
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher ui, open the Prompt tab.
scenarios.do: Paste a risky prompt intended for Claude Desktop chat or Codex Desktop.
scenarios.expected: Same preflight logic in a local Companion/Prompt widget: risk, reasons, expected impact, editable brief, copy brief or original. POST /api/preflight serves the same contract for future extensions. Widget copy names actual non-hook surfaces and hook-status is required before claiming automatic desktop/browser coverage.
scenarios.value: Honest coverage for surfaces with no lifecycle hook — useful on its own, not pretend interception.
scenarios.why: Missing per README step 1: copy/paste ergonomics polish after beta feedback. That polish is now done; underlying widget/endpoint predates this and was unchanged.

scenarios.title: First-run setup gets a new user to first value
scenarios.go: Install AIWatcher Local for the first time with no existing local state.
scenarios.do: Run aiwatcher setup, or open the dashboard's Setup tab.
scenarios.expected: A short checklist walks through: starting the Companion, opening the Console, running doctor/coverage, installing hooks for detected surfaces, using hook-status to confirm a hook actually fired, running watch/scan, and doing a risky-prompt plus Fresh Start smoke test.
scenarios.value: Replaces guesswork about which of ~20+ CLI subcommands to try first with one guided pass to first value.
scenarios.why: Before this, a new developer had to already know AIWatcher's command surface to get any value from it -- defeating the point of a desktop-first, zero-config local tool.

scenarios.title: Context health surfaces during long sessions
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher watch --once during or after a long high-context session.
scenarios.do: Review context growth and session signals.
scenarios.expected: Every poll now runs context-health severity (warning/critical) with compact guidance for the latest session, and separately for every other session in the window (not just the latest, as originally) -- surfaced in the 'Other sessions with local signals' list too. Still polling-based (README step 3's 'live' framing), not a push notification -- watch's own header says 'local logs only, not a live feed.'
scenarios.value: Prevents quality degradation from bloated sessions.
scenarios.why: Watch must move from periodic to live before loop/runaway control can sit on it. Manually verified via `aiwatcher watch --once` against real local session history.

scenarios.title: Critical context opens Fresh Start continuation
scenarios.go: Run the Companion/watch against a CRITICAL-context or severe-loop session, or open session review / Fresh Start manually from the Console.
scenarios.do: Put unrelated text on the clipboard, then click Fresh Start from the Companion or session drawer.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher recommends Fresh Start only for credible context/severe loop pressure, shows identity confidence, asks Replace before overwriting unrelated clipboard content, then copies a task-first brief and shows a visible copied/proof-pending confirmation. Workspace/tool opens only when runtime attachment is verified; full evidence enrichment can load afterward.
scenarios.value: Restart without losing state, hijacking the wrong app, or accidentally replacing a user clipboard.
scenarios.why: Same continuity engine powers restart, lane switch, and receipt proof.

scenarios.title: Low runway triggers lane switch
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher watch --once while one tool is under heavy trailing-5h usage relative to its own baseline.
scenarios.do: Compare the recommended action against manually running resume --target codex --copy.
scenarios.expected: _runway_pressure() estimates trailing-5h usage vs. the tool's own p75 baseline (claude-code/codex-cli only -- no baseline exists for Cursor, so no guess is made for it). At >=1.5x, watch's recommendation now names a concrete alternate tool (claude<->codex swap) and emits the exact `aiwatcher resume --session-id ... --target ... --copy` command to run -- not just a ratio with no next step. Always labeled 'local estimate, not a real-time quota API', never live.
scenarios.value: Avoids subscription pause frustration. The screenshot feature.
scenarios.why: Quota runway and API spend are separate meters — both now visible, neither yet predictive.

scenarios.title: Watch signals reach the developer without manual CLI polling
scenarios.go: Run AIWatcher with the small Companion while working in Claude, Codex, Cursor, or VS Code.
scenarios.do: Use Scan on demand and continue a session until context health, runway, loop, velocity, or prompt-gate pressure appears.
scenarios.expected: One durable intervention record drives Companion/dashboard delivery. The Companion stays small and draggable, highlights the relevant Plan/Control/Watch action, shows one primary action plus Skip/Console, and quiets after skip, continue, copy, or viewed receipt. Duplicate visible delivery is suppressed unless severity worsens or snooze expires.
scenarios.value: AIWatcher is present during work without becoming a noisy second dashboard.
scenarios.why: PR23 built the CLI Watch engine; PR37 (closes issue #31) delivered the OS-notification + dashboard-deep-link half. Daily OSS value needs delivery in the user's workflow, while staying honest about platform limits.

scenarios.title: Runtime hygiene identifies stale local AI runtimes
scenarios.go: Leave old Codex/Claude/Cursor/node_repl/Computer Use runtimes around, including orphaned PPID=1 or stopped processes.
scenarios.do: Run aiwatcher processes --stale-only and review the suggested cleanup candidates.
scenarios.expected: Read-only process metadata only: PID, age, state, runtime label, RSS/CPU, session/workdir flags, and stale reason. No prompt text, source, process memory, raw command line, upload, or auto-kill. `aiwatcher processes` (with --stale-only, --json) is implemented in main and matches this field list exactly. Still missing: dashboard UI surfacing -- no Coverage/Today card shows runtime hygiene yet, CLI-only today.
scenarios.value: A daily local hygiene check that explains abandoned agent runtimes without overstating AI spend savings.
scenarios.why: This is Watch/Control hygiene for the laptop: fewer stale sessions, less CPU/RAM/battery confusion, and clearer local state before starting new AI work. Command shipped 2026-07-24; this status previously said the command itself was missing from main, which was already stale.

scenarios.title: Vendor auto-compact is recorded as context event
scenarios.go: Run a long Codex or Claude session that triggers vendor context auto-compaction, or mark that compaction happened manually.
scenarios.do: Open Today/session detail or generate a Fresh Start brief.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher labels the event as Context compacted, stores confidence/evidence source, and recommends Fresh Start when the work is risky, multi-file, failing tests, or ready to switch tools. Fresh Start continuity exists today; missing: auto-compact event detection and UI badge/action.
scenarios.value: Built-in compaction keeps the model moving; AIWatcher keeps the work resumable, portable, and provable.
scenarios.why: Do not compete with vendor memory management. Complement it with continuity and evidence when compression is not enough.

scenarios.title: Gate allows original
scenarios.go: Trigger S-02.
scenarios.do: Click Run original.
scenarios.expected: Original prompt proceeds. Decision recorded locally as run_original with hash, not text.
scenarios.value: User autonomy with audit trail.
scenarios.why: Control should not remove agency.

scenarios.title: Gate adds safer brief
scenarios.go: Trigger S-02.
scenarios.do: Click Add safer brief (or Add edited brief).
scenarios.expected: Brief added as controlling context beside the original request. Decision + predicted impact recorded. Edited briefs tunable locally before adding.
scenarios.value: Concrete safer execution path.
scenarios.why: This is the core behavior change. Hook adds context; it cannot replace text — the four-option wording reflects that.

scenarios.title: Gate cancels run
scenarios.go: Trigger S-02.
scenarios.do: Click Cancel run.
scenarios.expected: Prompt does not execute; blocked decision recorded.
scenarios.value: Hard stop for bad work.
scenarios.why: Sometimes the best control is not running.

scenarios.title: Web prompt interception — OPEN DECISION
scenarios.go: Decision 1 pending: verify existing extension, or retire in favor of Prompt Companion + /api/preflight thin client.
scenarios.do: If Option A: load extension, submit risky prompt on claude.ai. If Option B: update suite, README, scope to one story.
scenarios.expected: Option A: overlay before send with brief replacing textarea. Option B: S-08 becomes a Companion flow + future extension scenario.
scenarios.value: True web interception is the strongest coverage claim; the API-contract route is the better architecture.
scenarios.why: Suite said built-and-wired; README says non-hook surface. Held at To test until decided.

scenarios.title: Codex prompt receives brief
scenarios.go: Run install-codex-hook --write --scope user; open Codex, run /hooks and trust the command.
scenarios.do: Submit risky prompt.
scenarios.expected: hook-status records invocation; Codex receives execution brief as additional context (or gate with --gate). Note: Codex Desktop chat verified NOT invoking — CLI/TUI only, host-build-dependent.
scenarios.value: Codex coverage without an explicit aiwatcher command every time.
scenarios.why: Cross-tool positioning depends on this. Per-session savings need rollout token_count events; cumulative-only records stay visible but excluded from estimates.

scenarios.title: Cursor composer is protected
scenarios.go: Install Cursor hook.
scenarios.do: Submit risky prompt in Cursor composer.
scenarios.expected: Cursor blocks the risky submission and returns a scoped brief for resubmission. Cannot rewrite composer text in place — paused gate, honestly described.
scenarios.value: Editor-native guardrails.
scenarios.why: Verified boundary per repo. Token/cost detail intentionally limited until Cursor exposes it locally — labeled, not guessed.

scenarios.title: MCP soft preflight presents options
scenarios.go: Register AIWatcher MCP and instruction file. Open Claude Desktop general chat.
scenarios.do: Ask a risky task.
scenarios.expected: Claude calls preflight tool, shows risk, safer brief, predicted impact, and waits for A/B/C choice.
scenarios.value: Best available Desktop-chat coverage when no hard hook exists.
scenarios.why: Must not overclaim automatic interception. Verify the tool call actually fires.

scenarios.title: Loop detection offers stop
scenarios.go: Create repeated edit/test failure loop, then run aiwatcher watch --once or --interval.
scenarios.do: Let agent repeat same file/test cycle 3+ times.
scenarios.expected: Done: watch polling detects repeated identical tool-call content (content-hash matching), shows tokens/cost burned across the repeats, and at severe repeat counts (5+) prepares a Fresh Start brief seeded with the loop diagnosis as the leading warning. Still missing: a true one-keystroke live stop of an actively-running session -- watch re-scans local logs on a timer, it does not hook into or interrupt a running agent process. That would need genuinely different plumbing (live process hooking, not periodic log scanning) and is deliberately deferred as separate, explicitly-scoped future work, not attempted as part of this batch.
scenarios.value: Stops waste while it is happening.
scenarios.why: Preflight cannot catch loops that form during execution. Depends on live-watch rework (README step 3).

scenarios.title: Runaway velocity alert
scenarios.go: Create high tokens/minute session with no progress signals, then run aiwatcher watch --once.
scenarios.do: Continue session past threshold.
scenarios.expected: Done: watch polling computes tokens/minute over the trailing 10 minutes vs. the user's own per-tool p75 baseline (real historical session data, not an assumed rate); at >=2x it drives the recommended action to 'narrow scope' with the exact ratio shown, always labeled a local estimate. Still missing: interactive pause/stop/set-cap controls with decisions recorded during an actively-running session -- same live-process-hooking gap as S-17, deliberately deferred as separate future work.
scenarios.value: Prevents invoice or quota shock at minute five, not on the bill.
scenarios.why: Velocity is independent of prompt risk. Baseline improves automatically as history accumulates.

scenarios.title: Dangerous command gate — reinstated
scenarios.go: Install via aiwatcher install-claude-command-gate, then give the agent a task that leads to a blocklisted command (rm -rf, git push --force, git reset --hard, credential/env reads, prod connection strings).
scenarios.do: Watch the PreToolUse gate open; choose Allow once / Block / Always-allow-this-pattern.
scenarios.expected: Command intercepted at PreToolUse time via a real Claude Code hook. Gate shows exact command, why flagged, and Allow / Block / Always-allow-this-pattern. Decision recorded with full command text (an intentional, documented exception to the general prompt-hash-only privacy rule -- a shell command is not private the way a prompt is). Deliberately Claude Code only: Codex/Cursor PreToolUse-equivalent hook schemas were unverified, and guessing at them was explicitly rejected in favor of shipping a real, working gate for one platform. Note: the S-19 manual-verification command referenced elsewhere in planning docs (a risky *prompt* like 'delete all files') exercises the separate prompt-preflight path (S-03/S-04), not this command gate -- only an actual blocklisted tool call triggers it.
scenarios.value: Protects when the agent does something the prompt never revealed. The launch screenshot.
scenarios.why: Fell off the README roadmap (Decision 2). Cheapest control win: interception point exists today, gate UX exists today. Always-allow-pattern required to avoid nag fatigue.

scenarios.title: Host-generated payloads are classified before Prompt Gate scoring
scenarios.go: Trigger a host lifecycle event (e.g. a Claude Code task-notification payload) and, separately, let AIWatcher deliver its own execution brief or Fresh Start brief back through a hook response.
scenarios.do: Inspect the resulting hook event via aiwatcher hook-status and confirm neither is treated as a raw user prompt.
scenarios.expected: Host task-notification-shaped payloads are always risk-scored (never silently skipped) but labeled host_task_notification so Prompt Gate framing doesn't ask 'did you mean to ask this?' about text nobody typed. AIWatcher-generated briefs skip re-scoring only when they carry a live, single-use token minted by issue_brief_token() at actual delivery time and verified by consume_brief_token() -- the previous static marker-string check (public in this OSS repo, so spoofable) no longer grants a bypass on shape alone. Token read/write failures fail soft toward scoring, never toward skipping it.
scenarios.value: Closes a real Prompt Gate bypass: static marker strings that anyone reading this repo could prepend to a prompt no longer skip risk scoring.
scenarios.why: Found and fixed via review on PR #37 (Finding 1): _classify_hook_prompt_source and the brief-resubmission check trusted public, guessable text shape alone. A per-instance, single-use token cannot be forged from the source alone.

scenarios.title: Intervention receipts link decision to result
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher ui after a gate decision.
scenarios.do: Open Receipts/Today; click into the session.
scenarios.expected: Receipt links decision → observed session usage, risk reduction, and outcome when linkable. Hashes, not prompt text.
scenarios.value: Evidence of AIWatcher impact.
scenarios.why: Prove phase needs a local ledger, not memory. Hook-provided session_id (Claude/Codex/Cursor, when the payload includes it) now links deterministically; correlate.py tool+project+time heuristic remains the fallback for hooks that do not supply one. The Receipts UI does not yet distinguish a hook-verified link from a heuristic-matched one (tracked separately).

scenarios.title: User marks outcome
scenarios.go: Complete or inspect a session.
scenarios.do: Run aiwatcher outcome useful (or rework/abandoned), or click Review outcome in UI.
scenarios.expected: Outcome recorded and reflected in Today/session views. Stored only on the laptop.
scenarios.value: Manual fallback and correction path for the quality signal.
scenarios.why: Manual is the override, not the primary — inference (S-24) leads.

scenarios.title: Session evidence links to code artifacts
scenarios.go: Run AI session in a git repo; change or commit files.
scenarios.do: Open session review.
scenarios.expected: Durable evidence snapshot stored: commit SHAs, hashed file paths/test artifacts, confidence, inferred outcome, survival timestamps (7/14/30-day buckets), revert/churn status, same-file re-prompt flag. No diffs, prompt text, commit subjects, or file contents in that durable store (regression-tested). Note: the transient, request-scoped evidence used to render the local session drawer does show real file paths and commit subjects/bodies -- a deliberate, documented choice (a commit message is written to explain a change to a future reader, unlike a prompt) that never leaves the machine and never reaches the durable store. Durable vs. transient scope confirmed by an independent audit, not just self-review.
scenarios.value: The dataset no one else can collect — the session and the repo on the same machine.
scenarios.why: P1. Foundation for measured outcomes and the intervention graph.

scenarios.title: Cost per surviving change
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher report --days 7, or open the dashboard once 5+ survival-checked sessions exist.
scenarios.do: Compare cost per surviving vs. cost per churned change.
scenarios.expected: Cost per surviving change computed at the 7/14/30-day buckets via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` (reachability, not just object existence -- avoids the 'dangling but not GC'd' false positive). Honesty-gated: shows nothing until >=5 survival-checked samples exist, rather than a number built on too little data. Surfaced in both the dashboard and the CLI weekly digest.
scenarios.value: Measures value, not token volume. Fixes the denominator every dashboard gets wrong.
scenarios.why: P3 rendering on P1 collection. No claim before the history exists.

scenarios.title: Weekly digest — costs and security in one card
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher report --days 7 or open Insights.
scenarios.do: Review the week.
scenarios.expected: One report now shows: outcome breakdown (useful/rework/abandoned + inferred), highest-cost useful session, a top-sessions list (costliest individually, regardless of outcome), loop/runaway candidates, command-gate fired/blocked counts, risky-prompts-modified count (flagged vs. actually taken safer), cost-per-surviving-change (measured, evidence-gated -- see S-23), and one priority-ordered recommendation. No unlabeled estimates shown. Minor gap: full per-tool spend breakdown exists in the dashboard's JSON API but the CLI text view still only shows the single top tool, not a full table -- pre-existing, not addressed in this batch.
scenarios.value: Turns the Ledger into a Monday ritual. The habit asset.
scenarios.why: Promoted to P2: 70% built, needs no outcome history to be useful day one.

scenarios.title: Passive evidence backfill
scenarios.go: Have older sessions without evidence snapshots.
scenarios.do: Run today, watch --once, or open the dashboard.
scenarios.expected: A capped batch of missing evidence snapshots is captured automatically — no daemon, no manual drawer clicks. Privacy rules identical to live capture.
scenarios.value: The intervention graph accumulates passively. The flywheel spins even when the developer does nothing.
scenarios.why: The most important compounding decision in the repo: history becomes evidence retroactively, within the cap.

scenarios.title: Privacy contract validation
scenarios.go: Fresh clone; run the README validation script end to end.
scenarios.do: Run start/today/tools/projects/report/sessions/resume/export/ui while monitoring network.
scenarios.expected: No API key requested. No network calls. Installed tools detected; limited-data tools honestly labeled, not guessed. JSON/event exports contain metadata, aggregates, and hashes — never prompt text or source. Real project folders, not parents. Time-window selector visibly updates.
scenarios.value: The trust posture made testable. A validation no cloud competitor can ship.
scenarios.why: 'If AIWatcher Local cannot explain what it reads and why, it should not read it' — this scenario is that sentence as a test.

scenarios.title: Daily journal gives a same-day recap
scenarios.go: Have at least one local AI session recorded today.
scenarios.do: Run aiwatcher journal, or open the dashboard's Daily Journal card.
scenarios.expected: A daily rollup shows session count, total cost/tokens for the window, the top project by cost, the single costliest session, a context-pressure/loop signal drawn from that day's sessions, and one specific 'thing to change next time' recommendation -- distinct from and complementary to the weekly digest (S-26).
scenarios.value: A same-day feedback loop instead of waiting for the weekly digest -- useful mid-week course correction.
scenarios.why: render_journal() and the dashboard's Daily Journal card already exist and are exercised daily, but had no scenario recording what they're supposed to show.

scenarios.title: Decision log entries carry rationale into Fresh Start briefs
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher log-decision --summary '...' --reasoning '...' --rejected '...' against a local session.
scenarios.do: Generate a Fresh Start brief for that same session (aiwatcher handoff/resume or the dashboard Fresh Start drawer).
scenarios.expected: The decision is stored locally as self-reported text (session_id, summary, reasoning, up to 5 rejected alternatives -- an intentional, documented exception to the prompt-hash-only privacy rule, same reasoning as S-19's command text), capped and rotated. It is not verified against what actually happened -- callers must label it as self-reported. The Fresh Start brief for that session includes the logged decision(s), so a fresh session inherits the 'why', not just the 'what'.
scenarios.value: Captures reasoning that never produces a commit (an approach seriously considered and rejected without being implemented) and carries it forward into the next session instead of losing it.
scenarios.why: This is the command referenced by AIWatcher's own recommended CLAUDE.md convention (install-claude-decision-log) and used in daily practice, but had no scenario covering it or its handoff integration.

scenarios.title: Session timeline stays privacy-safe
scenarios.go: Run a local AI session with several events (tool calls, edits, etc.).
scenarios.do: Run aiwatcher timeline --session-id <id>.
scenarios.expected: The timeline shows only metadata per event: timestamp, event type, model, token counts, cost, and a truncated content hash -- never prompt text, file contents, or raw command output. Verified by direct source read of render_session_timeline(): no field it prints originates from raw content.
scenarios.value: Lets a developer diagnose why a session got expensive (which event, how repeated) without re-exposing anything private.
scenarios.why: The command's own help text calls this 'a privacy-safe event timeline' -- exactly the kind of claim S-31's privacy contract validation should be checking, but S-31 never names it explicitly.

scenarios.title: Automatic outcome inference
scenarios.go: Complete a session with local evidence.
scenarios.do: Open Today/session review.
scenarios.expected: Done: inferred outcome with confidence and one-click confirm/correct appears from commits/tests/changes; churn/revert detection (a commit that looked useful gets downgraded if it didn't survive); same-file re-prompt signal (a later session touching the same files within 72h flags rework). Verdict rule confirmed by an independent audit: the codebase never infers a confident 'wasteful' outcome anywhere -- only useful/needs_review/churned. Still missing: platform-specific evidence weighting (confirmed absent by direct search, not just unverified) -- Claude/Codex/Cursor evidence is currently weighted identically, README step 4.
scenarios.value: Zero-effort ground truth; reduces labeling and makes useful work measurable.
scenarios.why: P1 with S-22. Verdict rule: 'needs review' when confidence is low — never a confident 'wasteful' without listed evidence.

scenarios.title: Non-code proxy outcomes
scenarios.go: Run a writing/analysis session.
scenarios.do: End session normally.
scenarios.expected: Proxy signals (copied output, revisit, abandonment, same-topic re-prompt) recorded with low confidence; one nudge for manual outcome.
scenarios.value: Extends value beyond code carefully, without pretending signals are equal.
scenarios.why: P3 by design. Noisy signals must not lead the outcome story.

scenarios.title: Search and resume previous work
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher sessions --search <term> --outcome useful --evidence needs_review --days 30.
scenarios.do: Find prior work by project/tool/model/id/file-topic/outcome/evidence; run resume --session-id <id> --target codex --copy or resume --outcome/--evidence --target ... --copy.
scenarios.expected: sessions/resume --search matches project/tool/model/session id, falling back to a 'rough topic' match against changed/touched file paths from local git evidence for anything that doesn't match those fields (never commit subjects or prompt text -- regression-tested). New --outcome (recorded useful/rework/abandoned) and --evidence (inferred useful/needs_review/churned) filters, usable alone or combined with --search. resume --session-id and one-click --target formatting (claude/codex/cursor/vscode/generic) already existed. The two previously-duplicated inline search matchers are now one shared filter_sessions() helper.
scenarios.value: Old AI work becomes reusable context. Search, resume, and Fresh Start make local history useful instead of archival.
scenarios.why: Daily utility requires retrieval and fast continuation, not just reporting.

scenarios.title: Install preserves existing hooks
scenarios.go: Have existing hook config.
scenarios.do: Run install-claude-hook --write --scope user; inspect settings.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher hook added without clobbering existing hooks; uninstall removes only AIWatcher.
scenarios.value: Trustworthy install.
scenarios.why: A local tool cannot break developer workflow.

scenarios.title: hook-status proves invocation
scenarios.go: Use any AI surface after installing hooks.
scenarios.do: Run aiwatcher hook-status.
scenarios.expected: Recent event = hook ran on that surface, showing whether prompt text was found and which risk score computed. No recent event = surface did not invoke the hook. Verified boundaries: Claude CLI + Desktop Code tab yes; Desktop general chat no; Codex Desktop no; Codex CLI/TUI build-dependent. Also shows the linked session_id when the hook payload provided one, directly proving which session a decision belongs to instead of relying on post-hoc correlation.
scenarios.value: Platform claims become provable instead of asserted. The arbiter for every coverage row in this suite.
scenarios.why: Not every surface uses the same hook runtime. Verify per surface, never per vendor name.

scenarios.title: Surface coverage explains automatic vs companion protection
scenarios.go: Install hooks, open Codex/Claude/Cursor/Desktop/browser surfaces, and run aiwatcher doctor plus hook-status.
scenarios.do: Compare each surface to what actually fired during a risky prompt.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher shows automatic, manual companion, read-only history, limited, or unverified per surface via `scanner.surface_coverage()` and the dashboard's Coverage tab. hook-status records action/result including skipped_internal and skipped_generated_brief (added by PR37/S-38) alongside passed, context_added, blocked, gate_opened, gate_failed, and prompt_missing.
scenarios.value: Users understand why Codex Desktop may not pop up even when logs exist, and know which fallback to use.
scenarios.why: Coverage honesty is part of the product moat. The tool should never let a user confuse session logs with active interception. Dashboard Coverage tab and the missing hook-status action/result detail both shipped in PR37.

scenarios.title: Home and Evidence rank session action items before charts
scenarios.go: Open AIWatcher Local after several sessions with mixed evidence quality.
scenarios.do: Review the top item and open its receipt.
scenarios.expected: Home/Evidence ranks actionable session, project, commit, receipt, Fresh Start, hook coverage, and evidence-quality items. Each row shows issue, suggested action, evidence label, privacy state, and receipt chain. Unknown/unverified/insufficient-data states are explicit. WorkUnit grouping is not shown as shipped OSS behavior.
scenarios.value: Creates a daily habit around useful AI work without making the developer interpret raw analytics.
scenarios.why: The OSS advantage is not another local spend dashboard; it is a private action loop that learns which interventions preserve durable outcomes.

scenarios.title: Intervention identifies the exact session before asking for action
scenarios.go: Run aiwatcher watch --notify/--overlay while multiple Claude/Codex/Desktop sessions exist in the same project.
scenarios.do: Trigger context, loop, velocity, or runway pressure and inspect the companion popup, dashboard Fresh Start bubble, session drawer, and Fresh Start drawer.
scenarios.expected: Every surface shows tool, surface, active/recent/historical state, project/worktree, last activity, short session id, and identity confidence. Only exact/active work interrupts. Likely or historical sessions appear as dashboard review items. App/workspace return is allowed only when verified; exact chat return remains unavailable unless the host provides a verified deep link or runtime handle.
scenarios.value: The user trusts the intervention because it names the work precisely and does not hijack the wrong chat.
scenarios.why: This is the first OSS moat layer: AIWatcher must know which live AI work is drifting before it can control or prove anything.

scenarios.platform: Dashboard + Native Companion + Fresh Start drawer
scenarios.title: Fresh Start provides one primary continuation action
scenarios.go: Open a critical-context session from the popup, Today Fresh Start bubble, or session drawer.
scenarios.do: Click the primary Fresh Start action with both an empty clipboard and a clipboard containing unrelated text.
scenarios.expected: There is one primary CTA: copy the Fresh Start brief, with explicit Replace confirmation before overwriting unrelated clipboard content. The brief is task-first, privacy-safe by default, includes fresh-chat/forked-chat/subagent continuation guidance, and is available before git/timeline enrichment finishes. Duplicate New chat / Copy handoff actions are not shown, and copied confirmation tells the user to paste into a fresh chat.
scenarios.value: The user continues work with less context drag while preserving clipboard intent.
scenarios.why: Fresh Start is the signature OSS experience: action bridge first, forensic detail second.

scenarios.title: Fresh Start receipt proves follow-up shape without overclaiming savings
scenarios.go: Copy a Fresh Start brief, start a later same-project session, then open Receipts.
scenarios.do: Inspect the latest Fresh Start receipt, click View receipt from the Companion, then Skip or close it.
scenarios.expected: Receipt shows proof status, correlation confidence, source -> follow-up tokens, API-equivalent value, model calls, tool calls, per-call metrics, outcome, commits/tests evidence, and notes that the comparison is observed so far, not a final savings claim. If no follow-up exists, it says proof pending and explains the missing evidence. Viewing or skipping the receipt quiets Companion attention until a new material signal appears.
scenarios.value: The user can see whether the intervention helped without being asked to believe a counterfactual.
scenarios.why: Receipts turn AIWatcher from advice into evidence.

scenarios.title: Session review and Fresh Start first paint stay usable on large local logs
scenarios.go: Use a machine with large Codex/Claude histories and open a heavy session or run aiwatcher sessions --days 1.
scenarios.do: Measure first visible content for session review and Fresh Start, then wait for detailed evidence enrichment.
scenarios.expected: Identity, usage, reason, and copyable basic Fresh Start brief appear before full timeline/git/prompt enrichment. The user can copy the basic brief without waiting; enrichment labels explain what is still loading. Windowed scanner paths avoid parsing obviously old/oversized nonessential Codex rows. Slow enrichment fails soft instead of blocking action.
scenarios.value: The product is usable during real work, not only on small demo histories.
scenarios.why: Speed is part of trust; a popup that leads to a slow blank drawer breaks the control loop.
